title: "Viability of deleting geom_fit and geom_add_slice_2d"
output: html_document
date: "2026-07-07"

# Verdict

**Both functions can be deleted; geom_slice supersedes them.** Nothing in
either implementation needs to survive — every capability they have is either
already in `geom_slice`, deliberately rejected in `decisions.Rmd`, or broken in
the original (three `gf_` cases are permanent KNOWN ISSUE failures that
`geom_slice` fixes). What *is* worth salvaging is smaller and cheaper: **5–7
test scenarios** that exist under `gf_`/`ga_` but have no `gs_` counterpart, a
couple of sentences from `geom_fit`'s documentation, and one **deletion
gotcha** (the package-wide `%>%` import lives in `R/geom_fit.R` but is needed
at runtime by `scatter_3d`).

This confirms the existing intent: `dev_todo.Rmd` already lists "deprecate
geom_fit", and `decisions.Rmd` ("geom_slice vs geom_add_slice_2d vs geom_fit")
already says the three should be one function. This report adds the concrete
salvage list and mechanics.

# Current status of the two functions

Both live in `R/geom_fit.R`. Neither is used anywhere else in `R/` — deleting
them breaks no internal code. The root `README.md` documents only
`geom_slice`; neither function appears in it.

**`geom_fit(model, new_data, resolution, color, interval, back_transform, se)`**

- Exported, with a full roxygen page (`man/geom_fit.Rd`).
- Pre-dates package conventions: `resolution` instead of `n`, a bespoke
  `color` argument instead of ggplot2 aesthetics, `new_data` (a data frame
  glued on with `cbind`) instead of `predict_vars`.
- Structurally naive: it takes the predictor from `model$model[[2]]`, so it
  only truly understands "the first predictor is x". With no `new_data` it
  cannot impute held variables at all — `gf_02`, `gf_09`, and `gf_10`
  (defaults, grouping, faceting) are KNOWN ISSUE cases that error with
  "variable lengths differ". `geom_slice` passes the equivalents
  (`gs_02`, `gs_07`, `gs_08`).

**`geom_add_slice_2d(model, xaxis, n, back_transform, color, ...)`**

- **Not exported and not documented** — no roxygen block, no Rd file. Only the
  test suite (via `devtools::load_all()`) and `testing/README.md` know it
  exists.
- Explicitly a stopgap: per `decisions.Rmd`, it was written during the early
  `geom_slice` struggles by wrapping `slice_2d`'s `prepare_slice_data()` in a
  single `geom_line()`. It has no grouping, no faceting (the same line repeats
  in every panel — see `ga_07`/`ga_08`, whose EXPECT headers are literally
  "review whether..."), no intervals, and `inherit.aes = FALSE` everywhere.
- Everything it does comes from `prepare_slice_data()`, which stays in
  `R/slice_2d.R` for `slice_2d`/`add_slice_2d`. Deleting the wrapper loses
  nothing and leaves the shared logic fully tested under `s2_`/`as_`.

# Anything valuable in the implementations?

Checked line by line; almost nothing. Points worth a decision:

1. **Full-range line.** `geom_fit` always draws across the model data's full x
   range; `geom_slice` draws across each *group's* plotted x range (a
   deliberate choice — "X Range" in `decisions.Rmd`). Not worth copying, but
   if the full-range behavior is ever missed, the ggplot2-idiomatic answer is
   a `fullrange` parameter like `geom_smooth()`'s. **Optional future feature,
   not a blocker.**
2. **Ribbon on by default.** `geom_fit` defaults to a confidence ribbon
   (mimicking `geom_smooth`); `geom_slice` defaults to `interval = "none"`.
   Keep `geom_slice`'s default (a slice is a line first), but it is a visible
   behavior change for anyone migrating — worth one line in `geom_slice`'s
   docs or the README migration notes.
3. **One `color` argument styles line + ribbon.** `geom_fit(color = "red")`
   colors both; `geom_slice(color = "red")` leaves the ribbon `fill` at its
   default, like `geom_smooth`. Correct behavior, but a migration footgun —
   worth a doc example (`geom_slice(model, interval = "confidence",
   color = "red", fill = "red")`).
4. `geom_add_slice_2d`'s implementation contains nothing `slice_2d` doesn't
   already have — it is eleven lines of glue.

Everything else (`back_transform` validation, inverse inference, prediction
grids, interval handling) exists in `geom_slice` in a strictly better form
(construction-time validation, named-string transforms, per-group pinning,
`pmin`/`pmax` ribbon flipping for decreasing transforms).

# Test cases: coverage map and what to port

`gf_` (28 cases) and `ga_` (23 cases) have **no reference images** — only `gs_`
does — so deleting them costs no ground-truth assets. The err-case snapshots in
`testing/expected/` (gf_24–28, ga_17–23) go with them.

## Scenarios already covered by gs_ (delete without replacement)

| gf_/ga_ scenario | gs_ equivalent |
|---|---|
| Single predictor (gf_01, ga_01) | gs_01 |
| Additive defaults/imputation (gf_02†, ga_02) | gs_02, gs_18 |
| Held values via new_data / `...` (gf_03, gf_07, ga_03) | gs_03, gs_04 |
| Quadratic (gf_04, ga_09) | gs_05 |
| Multiplicative / composite x-axis (gf_05, gf_06, ga_04, ga_05) | gs_19–gs_23 |
| Interaction, manual slices (gf_08, ga_06) | gs_06 |
| Interaction, grouped (gf_09†, ga_07‡) | gs_07 |
| Interaction, faceted (gf_10†, ga_08‡) | gs_08 |
| y-transform log / sqrt / inverse (gf_11, gf_15, gf_16, ga_10, ga_12, ga_13) | gs_09, gs_10, gs_11 |
| mtcars log model (ga_16) | gs_12–gs_14 |
| Confidence / prediction interval (gf_19, gf_20) | gs_33, gs_34 |
| `se = FALSE` (gf_22) | every default gs_ case (`interval = "none"` is the default) |
| err: non-lm (gf_24, ga_17) | gs_27 |
| err: nonexistent x variable (ga_18) | gs_28 |
| err: `$` names (gf_25, ga_20) | gs_29 |
| err: character variable (gf_26, ga_21) | gs_30 |
| err: invalid back_transform (gf_27, ga_22) | gs_31 |
| err: multi-arg back_transform fn (gf_28, ga_23) | gs_32 |

† KNOWN ISSUE case — permanently failing in geom_fit, *passing* in geom_slice.
‡ "Review" case documenting geom_add_slice_2d's known inability.

## Scenarios with NO gs_ counterpart — port before deleting

These are the actual value in the old suites. Each becomes a new `gs_` case
(with a reference image, per the gs_ convention):

1. **Explicit `back_transform` function** (from gf_12): model `1/y ~ x`,
   `back_transform = \(x) 1/x`, same curve as the auto-detected gs_11. Also
   nothing currently exercises the **named-string form**
   (`back_transform = "log"`), which only geom_slice has — one case for it
   would close that hole too.
2. **`back_transform = FALSE`** (from gf_14): transformed response plotted on
   the transformed axis with back-transformation explicitly off. gs_31/32 test
   invalid input; no case tests the valid opt-out.
3. **Transformed-axis match, non-log** (from gf_13): `1/y ~ x` plotted with
   `aes(x, 1/y)` — geom_slice should notice the axis equals the response and
   draw a straight line. gs_26 covers the log analog only; the inverse analog
   exercises the decreasing-transform path.
4. **y-transform exp and square** (from gf_17/gf_18, ga_14/ga_15): every other
   function family tests these (s2_12/13, as_10/11, dw_11/12); gs_ stops at
   log/sqrt/inverse.
5. **Both intervals on one plot** (from gf_21): confidence + prediction ribbon
   from two geom_slice layers, nested. Already on the dev_todo list.
6. **Real-data interaction with natural grouping** (from gf_23): the mpg
   `hwy ~ displ + I(displ^2) + displ:drv` plot. gf_23 needed three manual
   layers with hand-set colors; the gs_ version should be ONE
   `geom_slice(model)` with `aes(color = drv)` — a nice showcase case. Already
   on the dev_todo list ("gf_23 for gs, but with grouping and natural colors").
7. *(Optional)* **err: discrete x-axis** (from ga_19's factor-xaxis error):
   geom_slice aborts on a discrete x scale in `scale_transformation()`, but no
   gs_ case snapshots that message (gs_16 tests a factor predictor *off* the
   axis; ap_09 covers the autoplot side).

Items 1–4 are one-file cases mirroring existing gs_09–11 patterns; 5–6 were
already planned. This is roughly an afternoon of case-writing plus a
`testing/reference/build_all.R` run for the new references.

# Documentation worth carrying over

- `man/geom_fit.Rd` is generated; it disappears with the roxygen block.
  Nothing in it is missing from `geom_slice`'s page except one framing idea:
  geom_fit pitches itself as "**mimicking geom_smooth, but from your actual
  fitted model**". That contrast (geom_smooth fits its own loess/lm per panel;
  geom_slice draws *your* model) is the single best one-line explanation of
  why the package exists, and geom_slice's Rd/README never states it directly.
  Worth adding to `geom_slice`'s description and the README.
- geom_fit's example (two layers with `new_data = data.frame(group = "A")` /
  `"B"`) is exactly the workflow geom_slice replaces with `aes(color = group)`
  — good raw material for a "migrating from geom_fit" note if any users exist.
- `geom_add_slice_2d` has no documentation to salvage.
- `testing/README.md`: drop the `gf_` and `ga_` rows from the prefix table
  (and the `gf_24_err_non_lm` / "geom_fit" mentions in the err-case paragraph).
- `decisions.Rmd`: rewrite the "geom_slice vs geom_add_slice_2d vs geom_fit"
  section from "these should be combined" to a record that they *were*
  superseded and deleted (it also contains a typo-tangle where `geom_fit` is
  named three times meaning different functions — deletion resolves it).
- `for_devs/dev_todo.Rmd`: check off "deprecate geom_fit"; drop the "gf_11 /
  gf_21 / gf_23 for gs" bullets once the ports above land.
- Archived material (`testing/archive/*`, `geom_slice_progress.Rmd` history)
  mentions geom_fit; archives stay as-is.

# Deletion mechanics (checklist)

1. **⚠ Move the `%>%` import first.** `R/geom_fit.R` hosts
   `#' @importFrom dplyr %>%` — the only such tag in the package — and
   `scatter_3d()` needs `%>%` **at runtime** (it builds plotly calls via
   `eval(parse(text = "plot_ly() %>% ..."))`, evaluated in the package
   namespace). Deleting the file and re-roxygenizing silently drops the import
   and breaks `scatter_3d`. Either move the tag to `R/Applr-package.R` or
   refactor `scatter_3d` off the parsed-text pipe (the better fix; it also
   unblocks the "remove %>% in favor of |>" todo and lets `dplyr` leave
   DESCRIPTION's Imports entirely).
2. Port the test scenarios above (new gs_ cases + reference images +
   `--update` for any new console snapshots).
3. Delete `R/geom_fit.R` (both functions).
4. Re-roxygenize: removes `export(geom_fit)` and `man/geom_fit.Rd`. The
   `importFrom(ggplot2, geom_ribbon)` also drops out; `aes`/`geom_line` etc.
   are still imported via other files' `@import ggplot2`.
5. Delete `testing/cases/gf_*.R` (28), `testing/cases/ga_*.R` (23), and
   `testing/expected/{gf_24..gf_28, ga_17..ga_23}.txt` (12). Nothing else
   references case files — run.R and report.Rmd auto-discover.
6. Doc edits from the section above (testing/README.md, decisions.Rmd,
   dev_todo.Rmd, add the geom_smooth-contrast line to geom_slice's docs).
7. Full suite run: expect the pre-existing FAIL count to drop by three
   (gf_02, gf_09, gf_10 were known-broken by design).

# Delete outright or deprecate?

- **`geom_add_slice_2d`: delete outright.** Never exported, never documented;
  no user can be calling it.
- **`geom_fit`: delete outright, with a courtesy error stub as a cheap
  option.** It *is* exported, but the package is at version 0.0.0.9000, not on
  CRAN, and aimed at a single course; the README never mentions it. If any
  student code might call it, keep a 5-line stub for one release that
  `slice_abort()`s with "geom_fit() has been replaced by geom_slice()" plus a
  migration hint — the same pattern geom_slice already uses for its `xaxis`
  courtesy argument. A full `lifecycle`-style soft deprecation (working
  function + warning) is more machinery than a broken-by-design function
  deserves: three of its documented scenarios already error.
